note: Every entry was checked against the publisher's own pages or metadata on the date in checked_at. licence.commercialUse and access.automatable are separate facts on purpose: a dataset can be legally usable and still impossible to fetch without an account, or easy to fetch and illegal to republish.

classes.open-public-domain: No conditions; US Government work or equivalent.
classes.attribution-required: May be used and redistributed, including commercially, with attribution.
classes.noncommercial-only: Use is limited to non-commercial purposes; any product that earns revenue must ask permission first.
classes.terms-uncertain: No clear licence statement, or conflicting statements between a registry and a publisher.
classes.access-gated: Technically obtainable only with an account, an API key or a request form.
classes.inaccessible: No usable access method for an automated or scripted workflow.

sources.product: 3DEPElevation ImageServer (best-available lidar DEM, resampled on request)
sources.methodology: Airborne lidar and photogrammetric DEMs blended into a seamless bare-earth surface; the ImageServer resamples and reprojects server-side.
sources.resolution: 1 m where lidar coverage exists (Indiana, Kentucky and Illinois are complete), 10 m or 30 m elsewhere
sources.horizontalCrs: EPSG:4326 request and response, resampled from the native projection
sources.temporal: Static per acquisition; lidar flights in this region 2007-2023

access.rateLimits: not published; keep requests small and few

licence.name: U.S. Government work (public domain)
licence.attribution: courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey

limitations: Bare earth: no vegetation, buildings, fences or vehicles, so a low profile is not a clear view
Vertical accuracy describes the lidar source (about 0.1 m RMSE for QL2), not the resampled product served here
A server-side resample to a coarser grid smooths narrow ridges, levees and road cuts

sources.publisher: U.S. Geological Survey, Protected Areas Database of the United States, version 4.1
sources.methodology: Aggregated agency and NGO land records: owner, manager, designation, GAP protection status and an agency-reported public-access flag.
sources.resolution: Vector polygons as published by each agency; positional accuracy varies by source
sources.temporal: Version 4.1, 2024; each unit carries its own source date
limitations: Documents ownership, management, protection status and an agency access flag: not opening hours and not nighttime permission
Some units aggregate smaller parcels and are not survey boundaries
A gap in PAD-US is evidence of a gap, not evidence of private land

sources.publisher: Falchi, Cinzano, Duriscoe, Kyba, Elvidge, Baugh, Portnov, Rybnikova and Furgoni; GFZ Data Services
sources.product: Supplement to: The New World Atlas of Artificial Night Sky Brightness
sources.methodology: VIIRS DNB 2015 radiance propagated through an atmospheric radiative-transfer model (Cinzano and Falchi 2012) and calibrated against Sky Quality Meter measurements: artificial zenith sky radiance.
sources.units: mcd m^-2, artificial zenith sky brightness only

licence.name: CC BY-NC 4.0
licence.attribution: Falchi et al. 2016, GFZ Data Services, CC BY-NC 4.0

limitations: Artificial light only: the natural sky must be added before comparing with a meter
A model, not a measurement; accuracy is best at regional scale
2015 base year, so nine years of LED conversion and growth are missing
Not usable in a commercial product without permission from the authors
productionBlockers: access is manual and cannot be automated

sources.publisher: Earth Observation Group, Colorado School of Mines
sources.product: VIIRS Nighttime Lights annual V2.1 and V2.2 (average radiance, masked)
sources.methodology: Monthly cloud-free DNB averages combined into annual composites with outlier removal and a lit mask; radiance in nW cm^-2 sr^-1.
sources.units: nW cm^-2 sr^-1 (upward radiance at the satellite, not sky brightness)

access.authentication: account required for downloads; every data directory redirected to a sign-in page when checked

licence.name: CC BY 4.0 per the EOG product pages
licence.attribution: EOG, Colorado School of Mines; Elvidge et al. 2017 and 2021

limitations: Upward radiance is not sky brightness and cannot be converted without an emission and atmosphere model
Annual composites still contain gas flares, fishing fleets and industrial sources
The licence statement is on the product page while downloads sit behind an account whose terms are not published, so redistribution needs clarification before production use
productionBlockers: downloads require an account and the account terms are not verified

sources.publisher: World Bank Group, with NOAA/Colorado School of Mines and the University of Michigan
sources.product: Light Every Night: VIIRS DNB nightly imagery on AWS Open Data
sources.methodology: Nightly VIIRS DNB scenes as cloud-optimised GeoTIFF, per orbit, with monthly catalogues.

access.note: per-orbit scene files of 16-36 MB in lines/samples layout, so a regional mosaic is substantial work

licence.name: the registry states 'World Bank Open Database License (ODbL)' but links to CC BY 4.0
licence.redistribution: unclear; ODbL would impose share-alike on a derived database

limitations: The licence statement contradicts itself inside one registry entry
Per-orbit scenes are not analysis-ready; mosaicking and reprojection are required
Coverage effectively ends in 2020 for the study region
productionBlockers: licence statement contradicts itself (ODbL versus CC BY 4.0)

sources.methodology: Bidirectional-reflectance-corrected DNB radiance with lunar and atmospheric correction, composited annually.

access.method: LP DAAC and Earthdata Cloud, HDF5 tiles
access.note: automatable once an account exists; HDF5 needs a reader the prototype does not include

licence.name: NASA data policy: free and open, no restriction on use

limitations: Radiance, so the same non-convertibility applies as for any upward measurement
HDF5 tiles of about 10 MB at 500 m: a regional mosaic for one year is manageable, a national one is not
Requires an Earthdata account and token storage in the refresh job
productionNotes: legal and technically feasible, but the token must live in the refresh workflow and the mosaic must be precomputed, never fetched in a browser

sources.publisher: David J. Lorenz, University of Wisconsin-Madison
sources.product: Light Pollution Atlas 2025, a recomputation of the Cinzano/Falchi model on EOG VIIRS annual data
sources.methodology: The same radiative-transfer approach as the World Atlas, driven by the latest EOG annual composite and published as colour-scaled PNG maps.
sources.resolution: 1/120 degree (about 900 m) for continent maps, 1/40 degree for world maps
sources.units: artificial zenith sky brightness (mcd m^-2) shown as a colour ramp

access.method: PNG map downloads and an overlay viewer
access.note: no numeric raster download; the viewer tiles are not offered for bulk use

licence.name: no licence statement on the site; the author asks that the Bortle scale not be conflated with these maps

limitations: Only rendered images are published, so numeric sampling would mean reverse-engineering a colour ramp
Derived from EOG VIIRS, whose own access terms apply
The author states clearly that these are zenith brightness, not Bortle classes
productionBlockers: no numeric data product to sample

sources.product: OSM data through the Overpass API: roads, parking, access and fee tags
sources.methodology: Crowd-sourced mapping; tags describe physical features and, sometimes, legal access.

access.note: the public instance returned 503 under load during this research; the usage policy requires modest, cached, identified queries

licence.name: ODbL 1.0 for the database, with the OSM attribution guidelines
licence.shareAlikeNote: ODbL: a derived database must itself be offered under ODbL

limitations: A parking polygon does not establish that stopping there after dark is legal, or that a gate is open
Tag completeness varies, and a missing tag is not a missing restriction
Share-alike applies to a derived database, which matters if a candidate list is built from OSM geometry
productionBlockers: share-alike obligations for a derived database need a deliberate decision
tag values are not authoritative for legal access

sources.product: Property pages for state parks, state recreation areas and fish and wildlife areas
sources.temporal: Live pages, which may change without notice

licence.name: State of Indiana government publication: the fact of a stated opening time is quoted with attribution, and page text is not republished
licence.note: what is stored is the fact and a short quotation with its URL, not the page

limitations: Hours are stated per property and can be superseded by posted signs, alerts or closures
A page stating 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. means the property is closed at 11 p.m., whatever the sky is doing
productionNotes: store the quote, the URL and the retrieval date per candidate; never infer hours from a template

sources.publisher: USDA Forest Service, Shawnee National Forest
sources.product: Camping and cabins page, including overnight parking rules
limitations: Seasonal campground dates (typically 1 April to 15 December) and posted closures override the general rule
Day-use areas posted 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. are closed to overnight parking

sources.publisher: Mapzen/Joerd terrain tiles on AWS Open Data
sources.methodology: A blend of public-domain and openly licensed DEMs, tiled at zoom 0-15.
sources.resolution: About 30 m at zoom 12 in this region (SRTM and 3DEP blend)

licence.name: Mixed sources with a published attribution list
licence.attribution: United States 3DEP, GMTED2010 and SRTM courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey; full list on the project attribution page

limitations: Coarser than 3DEP in the United States, so it is a fallback rather than the primary
Attribution depends on which source feeds each tile, which the tile itself does not say
productionNotes: fallback only; the study region is fully covered by 3DEP at higher resolution

routing.name: OSRM public demo server
routing.verdict: not for production: the demo server is published for testing and carries no availability commitment

licence.name: demo server with no service guarantee and a policy against production use

routing.name: openrouteservice hosted API
routing.verdict: viable for a low-volume drive-time estimate with a key held server-side, at the cost of a new external dependency and a new secret to manage

licence.name: free tier with an API key, commercial plans available

routing.name: Self-hosted OSRM or Valhalla on a small VPS
routing.verdict: the honest long-term answer for road distance and drive time in one region: about 1-2 GB of RAM for an Indiana-scale extract, but it is a separate service outside the Cloudflare Pages architecture

licence.name: engine licences are permissive, the OSM data is ODbL

routing.name: Precomputed road-distance matrix from a one-off OSRM run
routing.verdict: the best fit for this product: a few thousand origin-destination pairs for one study area, generated offline and shipped as a small artefact, with no runtime service and no key

licence.name: derived from OSM (ODbL) by an OSRM run
licence.redistribution: ODbL share-alike applies to the derived database
